proof_summary: For odd prime \(p\), set \(T=2(p-1)\) and split the defining sum at \(T\): every term in the initial block contains either \(2^{p-1}-1\) or \(2^T-1\), hence vanishes modulo \(p\), while Fermat’s theorem and \(\binom{T+k+1}{2}-\binom{k+1}{2}=(p-1)(2k+2p-1)\) identify the shifted block with the original one. For \(p=2\), the recurrence \(a(n+1)=(2^n-1)a(n)+2^{\binom{n+1}{2}}\) shows inductively that all relevant terms are odd.
